title: SCA Minhag of the Week 250: "Noisemaking During the Reading of the Megilah"

chapters.title: Origins of the custom in France
chapters.about: Bet Yo'seif, Hot Hayim, Provence, 14th century, children banging rocks and wood

chapters.title: Customs in Italy and early opposition
chapters.about: Shibule Haleket, Italy, 13th century, banging feet and pots

chapters.title: Authorities opposing the noise
chapters.about: Rabbi Ya'aqob Al-Gazi, Rabbi Abraham Palaji, missing words of the Megillah

chapters.title: Customs in Egypt and the Middle East
chapters.about: Nehar Mitzrayim, Keter Shem Tov, 10 sons of Haman, Arur Haman

chapters.title: Customs in Halab and Argentina

chapters.title: Summary of the evolution of the custom
chapters.about: France, 12th century, spreading to Middle Eastern communities, avoiding disruption

summary: Mr. Morris Arking discusses the history and different customs of noisemaking during the reading of the Megillah across various communities and time periods. He reviews historical sources and rulings regarding whether and how children and adults should bang to erase the name of Haman.
questions: Where did the custom of banging during the Megillah reading originate?
Which early authorities and books recorded the custom of erasing Haman's name with rocks or wood?
Why did some rabbis oppose the custom of making noise during the reading?
What were the specific customs of banging in Egypt, Halab, and Argentina?
